promises.NothingPostsTwice: Nothing posts twice: one invite and one reminder of each tone to a person, one announcement, one close notice and one shared-with-you DM to each viewer.
promises.NoReminderAfterAnswer: No reminder posts to someone who has answered.
promises.ClosedIsToldOnce: Once a Holler closes, everyone with an unanswered DM sees it closed and its creator gets one close notice.
promises.ClaimedWorkIsNeverLost: Whatever was claimed is queued and posted, or given back for the cron to claim again, a viewer's shared-with-you DM included.
promises.KeptAnswersReachSlack: A person marked answered has a response, their latest DM thanks them, and the announcement counts it.

sending.says: One Holler, one person, one reminder: send, invite, remind, answer, close.

announcing.says: One Holler with an announcement channel: send, announce, answer, close.

answering-in-slack.says: As sending, with the answer tapped in Slack instead of sent on the web form.

closing.says: Two Hollers: send, invite, close, over overlapping passes.

sharing.says: One Holler, sent, whose creator shares it with its person and may remove them: add, queue, claim again, post.

claims-every-closed-holler.past: #10 claimed every closed Holler in one update before queueing the first, so one refusal left the rest claimed for good.

reminder-without-a-key.past: #10 posted a queued reminder without claiming a post key, so a reminder delivered twice posted twice.

announcement-never-retried.past: #10 had no pass for an announcement the queue refused, so the channel never got it.

conflict-queues-nothing.past: #22 kept an answer while the queue refused its thank-you, and sending again returned without queueing it.

keeps-refused-claims.removed: queueClaimed does not give claims back when the queue refuses them.

reminds-without-reading.removed: postToRecipient does not look at answered_at before it posts.

share-keyed-by-queue-time.removed: postKey names a share's queuedAt, so a share the queue took while its reply was lost, and the cron claimed again, has two post keys and posts twice.

close-before-they-send-again.finding: An answer is kept while the queue refuses its thank-you, and the Holler closes before the person sends again. recordResponse reads the status first, so answerOnWeb returns at closed and queues nothing. Their DM keeps asking for good: queueCloseWork skips it because they answered.

second-tap-skips-the-count.finding: An answer tapped in Slack is kept while the queue refuses its sends. The second tap is a conflict, and queueOutcome queues the thank-you without announce, so the announcement's count stays one short until the next answer.

close-lands-before-dm-ts.finding: A Holler closes while a consumer is posting an invite or a reminder. queueCloseWork reads who is waiting before dm_ts is stored, so that DM keeps its buttons after the close.

answer-lands-before-reminder-posts.finding: A person answers between postToRecipient reading answered_at and posting. The reminder reaches someone who has answered.

answer-lands-before-dm-ts.finding: A person opens the web form from the DM Slack just showed them and answers before its dm_ts is stored. The thank-you finds no DM to edit, so the question keeps asking.

queue-gives-up.finding: Slack fails for longer than max_retries: 6 retries and about ten minutes in apps/web/wrangler.jsonc. The queue drops the message, there is no dead-letter queue, and the claim (invited_at, reminders_sent, close_queued_at) stays, so no pass sends it again.

slack-loses-its-reply.finding: Slack posts and the reply is lost or is a 5xx page. postOnce cannot tell this from a failed post, gives the key back and posts again.

queue-loses-its-reply.finding: sendBatch queues the reminders and then throws. queueDueReminders gives the claims back and claims again with a new queuedAt, so the same reminder has two post keys and posts twice.

person-gives-up.finding: An answer is kept while the queue refuses its thank-you, and the person does not send again. Nothing in the cron repairs it, so their DM keeps asking for an answer Holler has.

worker-dies-in-go-live.finding: The Worker dies in goLive after marking the Holler live. It is live with no recipients, or with recipients claimed and never invited, and no pass looks for either.

worker-dies-in-queue-due-invites.finding: The Worker dies in queueDueInvites between setting invited_at and sendBatch. Those people are never invited.

worker-dies-in-queue-due-reminders.finding: The Worker dies in queueDueReminders between clearing next_reminder_at and sendBatch. Those people never get that reminder or a later one.

worker-dies-in-queue-close-work.finding: The Worker dies in queueCloseWork between setting close_queued_at and sendBatch. The unanswered DMs keep their buttons and the creator gets no close notice.

worker-dies-in-record-response.finding: The Worker dies in recordResponse between setting answered_at and inserting the response. Sending again is a conflict, so Holler thanks the person for an answer it does not have.

worker-dies-in-post-once.finding: A consumer dies between claiming a post key and posting. The queue delivers the message again, the key is taken, and it is acked without a post.

worker-dies-before-dm-ts.finding: A consumer dies between posting a DM and storing dm_ts. The person has the DM, but Holler never reminds them, thanks them in it or shows it closed.

worker-dies-before-announce-ts.finding: A consumer dies between posting the announcement and storing announce_ts. The channel keeps a count that never moves and never closes.

worker-dies-in-add-viewers.finding: The Worker dies in addViewers between inserting the viewer with notified_at and sendBatch. The cron reads only viewers with no notified_at, so that person never gets the shared-with-you DM.

worker-dies-in-queue-share-notices.finding: The Worker dies in queueShareNotices between setting notified_at and sendBatch. That person never gets the shared-with-you DM.
